p102.002: To a materialist who does not believe in God, a human being is nothing but an accident. Human love, hope, and faith are just reactions that matter happened to produce, and even the labors of the finest person vanish forever at death. But The Urantia Book says this is not man's true destiny; it is only the cry of despair of a soul lost in spiritual darkness.
p102.003: All this darkness and despair is swept away forever by one brave reach of faith from even the humblest and least educated child of God on earth. This saving faith is born in the heart when a person realizes that human values can be moved from matter to spirit, from man to God, and from time to eternity.
p102.005: The Thought Adjuster (the spirit of God who lives within our minds) changes our simple sense of duty into a sure faith in eternal truth. Whoever chooses to do God's will comes to know the way of truth. The Urantia Book says, “⟦Q 102:1.1⟧Human things must be known in order to be loved, but divine things must be loved in order to be known.⟦/Q⟧” And it adds that honest doubts and sincere questions are not sin. We enter the kingdom of heaven with the trust of a little child, but to keep growing we need the strong faith of a grown-up.
p102.006: The Urantia Book says that the more science you know, the fewer things you can be sure of, but the more religion you have, the more sure you become. The certainty of science comes from the intellect, but the assurance of religion comes from the whole personality. God is not proved by miracles or by material evidence. We come to know him by trusting him, and our hungry souls are satisfied by nothing less than knowing the living God directly.
p102.008: When we see true religion in someone else's life, we recognize it. Truly religious people are strong in their assurance, yet humble and self-controlled, and they do not push themselves forward. They live as if they were already living in eternity, and even in the rush and stress of the world they show a calm that does not waver. Knowledge is something we keep learning without end, but a spiritually awakened soul can say right now, ‘I know.’
p102.009: The Urantia Book says that true religion always acts. Lazy people hide behind rigid doctrines, and fearful people try to use religion as a shelter to escape from the hardships of life. But the mission of religion is to prepare people to face the changes of life with courage. Religion is never satisfied with thinking alone, or with feeling that does not lead to action. Religion is alive and on the move.
p102.011: A lack of education can make it harder for faith to grow. But The Urantia Book says that while human emotion often leads to selfish actions, religious insight leads to actions that serve others. A person who has found God goes out to serve his neighbors, not to show off his joy, but to share his overflowing goodness.
p102.012: The Urantia Book compares science, philosophy, religion, and revelation like this: science shows us facts, religion shows us values, philosophy shows us harmony, and revelation shows us true reality. Science classifies people, religion loves people as itself, wisdom treats them fairly, and revelation shows that man is a being who can work together with God. The Urantia Book also says that evolution tries to make God like man, but revelation tries to make man like God.
p102.014: Because the Thought Adjuster lives within us, knowing the mind of God is no more mysterious than knowing the mind of another person. We realize early on that we are not alone in this world, and faith widens this natural awareness into a religion that knows God. If God were not a person, he could not become part of a person's living religious experience.
p102.015: The Urantia Book says that today's religions stress prayer but neglect the more important matter of worship. “⟦Q 102:4.5⟧Prayer may enrich the life, but worship illuminates destiny.⟦/Q⟧” Spiritual experience is the real soul of the universe as we see it.
p102.017: The Urantia Book says that the religion of primitive people was closer to fear than to faith. But the fact that this fear has gradually changed into reverence for God and living faith is evidence that a higher possibility was hidden within it from the beginning.
p102.018: Morality can recognize values, but it is religion that keeps them, lifts them up, and makes them spiritual. The Urantia Book says the relationship between religion and morality is like the relationship between love and duty, or between a son and a servant. Morality shows us an almighty ruler to be served, but religion shows us a loving Father to be worshiped and loved.
p102.020: The progress of science and philosophy tears down the false gods that people have made. That may cloud spiritual vision for a while, but in the end it clears away the ignorance and superstition that hid the living God of love. The Urantia Book says that cutting off one part of life and calling it religion ruins both life and religion, and that God wants all of us. Love is the essence of religion and the source of higher civilization.
p102.021: The Urantia Book says that to science God is a possibility, to philosophy a probability, but to religion a certainty. The soul that knows God can boldly say, “⟦Q 102:6.5⟧I know⟦/Q⟧”. To anyone who doubts this, it can answer, “⟦Q 102:6.5⟧How do you know that I do not know?⟦/Q⟧” The most convincing evidence of this assurance is the fruit of love that believers bear. Jesus said that if we love one another “⟦Q 102:6.7⟧as I have loved you⟦/Q⟧”, all people will know that we are his disciples. The Urantia Book says that the evolution of living things is a fact, but the fact that this evolution always moves upward means there is a Creator with a purpose.
p102.023: The Urantia Book says that trying to build a religion without God is like trying to get fruit without a tree. We cannot pray to a chemical formula, plead with a mathematical equation, or share love with a law. It is possible to live a good and honest life without believing in God, but such a life, though it bears social fruit, does not bear spiritual fruit.
p102.024: The Urantia Book says that finding faults and raising objections takes no great wisdom, but answering those questions takes far more wisdom. That is why many people are sure of God inside but are afraid to say so because of the voices that oppose them. But God is the most real fact, the most living truth, and the most loving friend, so we have every right to be most surely confident of him.
p102.026: The highest evidence that religion is real lies in human experience itself: the fact that a person full of fear and eager to live is willing to hand over his present and future completely to the one whom faith calls God. You can tell the level of a religion by looking at its morals and ethics. The Urantia Book says that personal faith has always led the way in moral progress, while institutional religion has always lagged behind. The prophets led people forward, and the theologians often held them back.
p102.027: The Urantia Book says that true religion does not lean on miracles but is built on personal experience. The highest religion of all was the life of Jesus. In his short life he was a man who sought God and found him completely, and in that life God also found man. When we too live trusting God as Jesus did, we will gain an assurance of faith that cannot be shaken.
p103.002: Where does the desire to seek God and to do what is right come from? This paper looks at the answer step by step. The religious nature of human beings is inborn from the start. First the adjutant spirits, the spirit helpers that help the mind grow, guide this nature, and then the Spirit of Truth and the Thought Adjuster, the spirit of God who lives within our minds, lead it to higher understanding. The Thought Adjuster is the “⟦Q 103:0.1⟧cosmic window⟦/Q⟧” through which we can glimpse God by faith.
p103.003: The Urantia Book divides the religions of the world today into four kinds: natural religion, which arose on its own and has evolved; revealed religion, in which truth was made known from heaven; the actual religion of today, which is a mixture of these two; and philosophic religion, which people have built through reason and philosophy.
p103.005: Because the same spirit of God lives in our minds, people can be one in spirit. But because everyone's personality is different, they cannot all interpret that spirit's leading in the same way. That is why there are so many different definitions of religion, more than five hundred of them. To keep your own religion from becoming narrow and selfish, it is good to learn about the many religious experiences of other people as well.
p103.006: Religion does not begin with believing something; it begins with seeking precious values. That is why people can easily agree on the goals they pursue even when what they believe is different. “⟦Q 103:1.4⟧Theology does not produce religion; it is religion that produces theologic philosophy.⟦/Q⟧” The Urantia Book calls this special sense that recognizes values within a person God-consciousness.
p103.008: Just as a baby grows for nine months before it is born, religion grows in the mind before we notice it. Some people are born again spiritually after great suffering and confusion, while others grow quietly and naturally. Either way, religion does not grow unless a person makes efforts and decisions of his own. Someone who grew up knowing a loving God should not look down on someone who found God only after going through a great crisis.
p103.009: A small child's first moral impulses are the desire to be just, fair, and kind, that is, the desire to help others. Early on, a child struggles between thinking only of himself and caring for others. When he overcomes his selfish impulse and chooses for the sake of others, that is the very first form of religious experience. We feel that the urge to care for others comes from somewhere outside ourselves, and in fact it does come from the Thought Adjuster. But if we care so much for others that we neglect ourselves too much, or are troubled by a mistaken conscience, sorrow and unhappiness can come instead.
p103.011: Primitive religion grew out of beliefs about spirits, dreams, and many superstitions, and out of the feeling that held clans and tribes together. In the group, people began to wrestle with whether to act for themselves or for the group, and even tribes without totem beliefs knew that their own interests and the group's interests were not the same. But the impulse of true religion does not come from the group; it comes from the presence of the spirit, which makes us unselfish.
p103.012: Religion gradually developed in a direction that valued morality instead of magic, and it is destined to grow at last into the service of God and man. Even in ages full of fear and superstition, the moral element never disappeared. Thanks to these two forces, human effort and the divine urge, religion has survived the upheavals of long ages.
p103.014: What makes a religious gathering different from an ordinary one is the atmosphere of communion, of being together with God. People long ago felt this fellowship as they shared food together, and the Christian Lord's Supper carries on that tradition. In such an atmosphere, the struggle between the selfish mind and the mind that cares for others rests for a while, and this becomes the beginning of true worship.
p103.015: When primitive people felt that they had grown distant from God, they tried to repair the relationship by offering sacrifices. Our ideals grow quickly, but our power to live them out grows slowly, so we often feel guilty. But our task is not to reach our highest ideals perfectly; it is to be faithful to our purpose of seeking God and becoming like him. Jesus did away with all sacrifices and ceremonies of atonement and taught that man is a child of God. God is a loving Father who looks not at our report card but at our motives and our hearts.
p103.017: The desire to help others was at first directed only toward those closest to us. Then, as civilization advanced, the circle of neighbors widened to the tribe and the nation, and Jesus widened it to all humankind, teaching us to love even our enemies. Deep in their hearts, people know that this teaching is right. If we are taught that this unselfish desire is nothing but a herd instinct, our ideals lose their power, but if we know that it comes from the spirit of God within us, we gain great courage.
p103.018: That does not mean we should ignore ourselves. The self has rights just as our neighbor does. Happiness comes when caring for ourselves and caring for others are well balanced. This balance is not fully reached in this short life, but the effort to become like God goes on after death, and every good thing we do now makes the next life richer. The idea that we will automatically become good people just by dying only invites laziness.
p103.019: In spiritual matters, a human being has free will and is the architect of his own eternal destiny. Spiritual growth happens best not when it is forced but when we are free. “⟦Q 103:5.11⟧Where the spirit of the Lord is, there is freedom.⟦/Q⟧” The church, too, should work for spiritual unity rather than forcing everyone to think the same way.
p103.021: When people observe the universe from the outside, physical science is born, and when they look at it from within themselves, theology is born. Philosophy is the effort to reconcile the differences between these two paths. Seen from outside, the universe looks like a machine; seen from inside, everything looks spiritual. So if we insist on only one side, we see the universe in a distorted way. What links matter and spirit is mind, and it is through the mind that we experience all of this.
p103.022: Science and religion find it hard to get along because we do not know the morontia world, the in-between stage between matter and spirit. In the morontia world there is a higher understanding called mota, which removes the differences between science and religion. People have tried to fill this gap with metaphysics, but that only made the confusion greater. That is why revelation is the only hope of filling the empty space. The best philosophy is built on the reason of science, the faith of religion, and the truth of revelation together.
p103.024: Science is kept up by reason, and religion by faith. Faith does not come from reason, but it is never unreasonable. On the way up to God, we will experience God within and keep on studying the energy and matter of the universe without. Learning in science does not end on this earth.
p103.025: Both science and religion must look at themselves without fear and admit that they are not yet complete. Nothing in this world can be proved absolutely. Science starts from the assumption that matter, motion, and life are real, and religion starts from the assumption that mind, spirit, and the universe are real. Science discovers the material world, religion evaluates its worth, and philosophy links the two and interprets their meaning. The presence of the Thought Adjuster in the mind is evidence of spiritual reality, but it is proved only to the person who experiences it.
p103.027: Science and philosophy can only say that God may possibly exist, but the personal experience of a spirit-led person can say that God surely exists. The ways people speak about God may differ and seem confusing, but the experience of God itself can be real.
p103.028: The Urantia Book explains this by comparing it to love. A man who loves his wife deeply might get a low score on a test about the psychology of love, but that does not make his love fake. So, it advises, if you believe in God and love him, do not let the doubts of science or the quibbles of logic shake that experience. The best philosophy avoids the extremes of seeing everything as only matter or everything as only God, and it recognizes the reality of personality.
p103.030: Religion is not just thinking; it is feeling, acting, and living. That is why a person's religion can be true and sincere even when his theology is mistaken. The Urantia Book counts early Buddhism among the finest religions without a God, but it says that a religion without faith is a contradiction. It also warns, “⟦Q 103:9.6⟧When theology masters religion, religion dies⟦/Q⟧”, because religion then becomes a rigid doctrine instead of a living life.
p103.031: Reason leads us into the world of facts, wisdom into the world of truth and relationships, and faith into the world of God. Faith goes along with reason as far as reason can go, goes with wisdom to the end of philosophy, and then sets out on an endless journey through the universe with truth as its only companion. True religion is more than a good feeling; it is an experience of believing and knowing, and its marks are faith in God, the hope of living forever, and above all, love for our neighbors. One small choice to give way for the sake of a friend is the very beginning of this kind of living religion.
p104.002: People have loved the number three for a long time. Our fingers have three joints, a stool stands on three legs, and for ages primitive people could not count beyond three. We often think in groups of three, such as yesterday, today, and tomorrow, or father, mother, and child. That is why many ancient peoples worshiped three gods. The Urantia Book calls this triadic belief and says it is different from the true Trinity made known by revelation. The Trinity means the one Deity formed by the union of three persons: the Universal Father, the Eternal Son, and the Infinite Spirit.
p104.003: The peoples of Persia, India, Greece, Egypt, Babylonia, Rome, and Scandinavia all worshiped three gods. Such groups of three gods arose naturally out of human experience, so they existed long before the true Paradise Trinity was made known. Later, this natural triadic belief and the revealed Trinity became mixed together, and in many cases it became hard to tell them apart.
p104.005: The Trinity was first made known on earth about half a million years ago through the staff of the Planetary Prince Caligastia, but it was forgotten in the confusion after the rebellion. The second presentation was by Adam and Eve, and the third was by Machiventa Melchizedek. Melchizedek used three concentric circles as his symbol, but most of his followers never really understood the union of Father, Son, and Spirit. This teaching spread to India and became the idea of being, intelligence, and joy, and teachings resembling the Trinity also arose in Buddhism. On the other hand, the Hebrews and the Muslims, who believed so strongly in one God alone, found it hard to tell the Trinity apart from the worship of three gods.
p104.006: Jesus also taught the Trinity to his apostles, but they understood it only as a figure of speech. Paul and the early church confused Jesus, the Creator Son of our local universe, with the Eternal Son of Paradise. The Trinity that Christianity accepted by the end of the first century was the Universal Father, the Creator Son of our universe, and the Mother Spirit of the local universe. The Urantia Book explains that this idea was wrong in some of its facts but true in its spiritual relationships, because the Creator Son fully shares the divinity of the Eternal Son, yet he is not the Eternal Son himself.
p104.008: Monotheism, the belief in only one God, grew up as a reaction against polytheism, in which many gods quarrel with each other. But when we picture a lonely God who has no relationship with anyone, it is easy to feel that God is a vague Absolute rather than a person. That is because personality shows itself in its relationships with other personalities. The Trinity shows us that within God there are equal persons who love one another.
p104.009: The Trinity is not a person, but it is a real reality. It is more than simply adding together the qualities of the three. For example, Jesus taught that justice is never the act of one person but always a group function. The Gods, too, do not carry out justice one by one but together, as the Trinity. Knowing about the Trinity helps us understand a little of how the love of God and the laws of the universe exist together.
p104.011: The Urantia Book explains that the reality of the whole universe is made up of seven Absolutes: the Universal Father, the Eternal Son, the Infinite Spirit, the Isle of Paradise, and the Deity Absolute, the Universal Absolute, and the Unqualified Absolute. These seven relate to one another and form the circle of infinity. Reason tells us that the universe is one, but our experience also shows us that it is many, always growing and changing.
p104.012: Here a new word appears: triunity. A triunity is a union that three form in order to work together, and it is different from the Trinity. The Trinity is a single Deity that cannot be divided, but a triunity is a working arrangement. There is only one Trinity, but there are many triunities. Still, the triunities are very real, and through them the Universal Father directly controls the great affairs of infinity.
p104.014: The Universal Father is part of all seven triunities. The first is the personal union of Father, Son, and Spirit, a union of love, mercy, and ministry. These three give us personality, spirit, and mind. The second is the union of pattern, which sets the design of all material things, from the smallest particle to the great stars and universes. The Urantia Book says that if love is the mark of the first triunity, pattern is the mark of the second. The third is the union of spirit, in which all spiritual things begin and end, and the fourth is the union that controls all energy, with Paradise as its heart.
p104.015: The fifth through the seventh are unions even harder for us to grasp, which bring about all the possibilities of the universe, the presence of God, and infinite unity. The Urantia Book reveals that there are fifteen triunities in all, but that eight of them have not been made known. The triunities are the “⟦Q 104:4.46⟧balance wheel of infinity⟦/Q⟧”, which lets infinity act as one even though it is divided into seven Absolutes. At the very center of all this is the Universal Father: “⟦Q 104:4.46⟧in him all things consist⟦/Q⟧”.
p104.017: There are also unions of three that do not include the Father, and these are called triodities. One is the triodity of actuality, made up of the Eternal Son, the Isle of Paradise, and the Conjoint Actor, which co-ordinates all reality that has already come into being. The other is the triodity of potentiality, made up of the three Absolutes, which ties together all the possibilities that have not yet been revealed.
p104.018: The triodities are closely connected with the appearance of the God who grows in time, the Supreme Being. To creatures like us, the Supreme Being is a revelation showing that the whole universe is one. This paper is hard, but one thing is clear: God is not alone and lonely but loves and works in relationships, and we too were made to grow together in relationships.
p105.002: This paper takes up one of the hardest subjects in The Urantia Book: where all reality began. Infinity is only partly understood even by the high beings of the universe, so our human minds cannot fully grasp it. The Urantia Book suggests that we picture eternity and infinity as a great ellipse, beginning from one absolute cause, branching out into endless variety, and then reaching back toward an infinite destination. And it attempts an explanation, even while knowing that much of the meaning may change in the process of putting it into terms on our level.
p105.003: 1. The Philosophic Concept of the I AM
p105.004: The philosophers of the universe call the first cause of all things the I AM. The I AM is infinite and eternal, and no limits of any kind can be placed on him. The Urantia Book asks us to imagine a moment in the far, far past. At that time nothing had yet been divided, and every possibility lay hidden within the I AM. Even so, there was within him the possibility of willing on his own.
p105.005: The important thing is that this I AM is the very same as the God we call Father. The God we know by experience is one part of infinity, and there is far more of God that we do not know. Even the endlessly vast universe shows only a small part of infinity. But the face that the Infinite turns toward all of us is “⟦Q 105:1.8⟧the face of a Father, the Universal Father of love⟦/Q⟧”.
p105.006: 2. The I AM as Triune and as Sevenfold
p105.007: The Urantia Book stresses that the absolute realities have all existed from eternity and have no beginning. It explains them as if in time order only to make them easier for us to understand. The I AM divides within himself into various relationships, and there are seven of these relationships in all.
p105.008: First, the I AM is the Father of the Eternal Son, that is, the Universal Father. Even people like us, still living in the flesh, can experience this aspect a little through worship. Second, he is the cause of Paradise, the Universal Controller who sets the pattern of all material things. The Urantia Book says, “⟦Q 105:2.6⟧The Universal Father is God-as-love; the Universal Controller is God-as-pattern.⟦/Q⟧” Third, he is the Universal Creator who, united with the Son, made the central universe of Havona. The other four aspects are connected with the three Absolutes: maintaining infinity, limiting himself, holding all future possibilities, and binding everything together into one. In him we all “⟦Q 105:2.11⟧live and move and have our being⟦/Q⟧”.
p105.010: These seven relationships are revealed eternally as the seven Absolutes. The First Source and Center, the Universal Father, is love, spirit, and energy, and he is the Father of all personalities. The second is the Eternal Son; no personality can reach the Father except through the Son. The third is the eternal Isle of Paradise, the center of all matter and gravity. Paradise is not in space; rather, space exists in relation to Paradise.
p105.011: The fourth is the Infinite Spirit, the Conjoint Actor, who weaves spirit and energy together and gives mind to all creatures. The fifth, the Deity Absolute, stands for all the possibilities of Deity yet to come, and the sixth, the Unqualified Absolute, stands for all the impersonal possibilities not yet revealed. The seventh, the Universal Absolute, links these two and bridges the tension between what already exists and what is not yet complete. All seven are eternal and without beginning, and all reality is built upon them.
p105.013: The Urantia Book explains this by borrowing an old saying: the one gives rise to two, the two give rise to three, and the three are the ancestors of all things. Within the oneness of the I AM, seven relationships arise; these seven relationships pair up with the seven Absolutes; and the Absolutes, working together in threes, form the triunities.
p105.014: Oneness is infinity itself, the relationships in pairs become the foundation of reality, and the unions of three make infinity actually work. Once the stage of the universe was set in this way, energy became varied, spirit spread out, and personality and mind were given as gifts.
p105.016: At first everything happened only on the absolute level. But when the Universal Father, by his own free will, limited himself, finite reality with its limits came into being. This was the beginning of universe history and of time. From then on, the great cycle of growth began, coming down from the heights of infinity into the finite world and then going back again toward Paradise and God.
p105.017: There are two kinds of finite reality. One is the worlds and beings that are perfect from the start, like Havona, and the other is the worlds and beings of the superuniverses, which grow and become perfect in time. What grows in time naturally looks imperfect for now, but in eternity this difference disappears. And as the two come together, a third kind of new values also comes into being.
p105.019: When the finite world appeared, many responses followed. Deity that grows in time, the Supreme, began to appear, and the physical organization of the seven superuniverses is still going on today. Also, along with the perfect beings of Havona, there came into being evolutionary beings who grow until they reach perfection.
p105.020: But growing toward perfection means not being perfect at first. The Urantia Book explains that here imperfection, disharmony, and conflict, that is, potential evil, arose. God fills in this imperfection through the work of God the Sevenfold. Because growth takes time, we can become God's partners and help complete the universe together with him. Even our material minds become partners with the Thought Adjuster in shaping an immortal soul.
p105.022: Between the finite and the absolute there is a level called the transcendentals. Transcendentals are beings and realities that are less than infinite but greater than finite, and they link the absolutes with finite things. The Deity called the Ultimate, the Architects of the Master Universe who designed the master universe, and things such as space belong to this level. Havona is not a transcendental, but because it is perfect without being absolute, it is a good example of this level.
p105.023: The universe we live in exists on three levels, finite, transcendental, and absolute, and on this stage the endless drama of personality and energy is played out. And all this variety is bound into one by the triunities, the Architects of the Master Universe, and the Seven Master Spirits. This paper is difficult, but the fact that everything began with a loving Father, and that we too are part of that great story, gives us great comfort and hope.
p106.002: A person ascending to God needs to know not only God, but also how he himself is related to the various realities of the universe. The Urantia Book explains reality by dividing it into seven levels. The first is the incomplete finite, still growing as we are, and the second is the maximum finite, which has reached the goal of the present age. Above these are the transcendental, which goes beyond the finite, the ultimate, which concerns the whole master universe, the coabsolute, greater still, the absolute, and the infinite, before all beginnings and after all endings.
p106.003: The Urantia Book says that this division is a simple one, made by necessity because of the limits of human language and mind, since there is so much we do not yet know. The seven superuniverses that are growing now will someday reach the age of light and life, and in the age after that, new growth will begin in outer space, farther away.
p106.005: Perfect Havona was perfect from the beginning, but the superuniverses where we live must grow little by little in time to become perfect. The Urantia Book says that this taking of time is actually a gift, because it lets creatures take part in their own growth and become partners of the Creators.
p106.006: During this long age of growth, God the Sevenfold helps us in our imperfection. God the Sevenfold is the sevenfold divine help that reaches from the Paradise Deities all the way to the Creator Son of our universe. No matter how far we are from Paradise, God the Sevenfold gives the love of truth, beauty, and goodness to creatures struggling there.
p106.008: If God the Sevenfold helps growth, the Supreme Being gathers the results of that growth into one. The Supreme Being is the God who grows in time and space, and he is completed as the power gained by all the evolution of the universe is joined with the spirit person who is in Havona. We mortals, too, are people who take part directly in this enormous work.
p106.009: Just as Michael of Nebadon reflects the perfection of the Paradise Father, we too will someday become close family of the Supreme Being and share in his perfection. Since God the Supreme grows through experience, we can come to know him fully through experience. And we can come to know the Father, the Son, and the Spirit as well, through prayer and worship.
p106.011: The Urantia Book explains how the realities on the transcendental level work together. The Architects of the Master Universe make the plans, the Supreme Creators carry them out, and the Supreme Being completes them. When this age ends, the Supreme Creators, the Supreme Being, and the Architects of the Master Universe will form a new union called the Trinity Ultimate.
p106.012: The Paradise Trinity is made up only of absolute Deities, but this new Trinity also includes the real experience of creatures. The Urantia Book says, “⟦Q 106:3.4⟧Group associations are enabled to anticipate, even to transcend, individual capacities⟦/Q⟧”. The principle that many working together can do what one alone cannot applies to the whole universe.
p106.014: The Trinity Ultimate will someday co-ordinate the entire master universe, and within it a Deity called God the Ultimate will appear more and more clearly. God the Ultimate is beyond time and space, but he is still less than absolute. The Urantia Book openly says that we cannot yet know what changes will happen when God the Ultimate fully appears. But every personality who took part in that process will experience the personal values of God the Ultimate.
p106.016: When God the Supreme and God the Ultimate appear, the foundation is laid for yet another union, the Trinity Absolute. This union is made up of God the Supreme, God the Ultimate, and the still unrevealed Consummator of Universe Destiny. This Trinity will be fully formed only after the whole master universe has been completed.
p106.017: Here The Urantia Book sums up again what a Trinity is. A Trinity is not itself a person, but it does not deny personality either. Its members are a Trinity only when they are together, not when each is on his own. And only Deities can form a Trinity.
p106.019: However vast the master universe is, it cannot hold everything absolute. The Urantia Book suggests that for the Trinity Absolute to work fully, an endless universe beyond the master universe may be needed. If so, the possibilities of the three Absolutes would gradually become real, and God the Absolute, the last of the Deities who grow through experience, might appear. The Urantia Book says there is little practical gain in a human trying to understand such far-off matters, yet it carefully shows us this possibility.
p106.021: Infinity can never be completely realized, no matter how much time passes, because there will always be possibilities in the three Absolutes that have not yet been revealed. So however much of God we come to know, there will always be more of God that we have not even guessed. The Urantia Book exclaims, “⟦Q 106:7.5⟧The quest for God is endless!⟦/Q⟧”
p106.022: This is not disappointing news but joyful news. We really can come to know God the Sevenfold, God the Supreme, and God the Ultimate, and the fact that God is infinite gives us the assurance that we will always have more to grow into and discover, forever. Even in the far future when the master universe is completed, we will look back on its whole history as only the beginning, and the universe will still seem young.
p106.024: The Urantia Book explains the Trinity of Trinities, in which three Trinities unite as one. On the first level, the Paradise Trinity, the Trinity Ultimate, and the Trinity Absolute work together, and on the second level, God the Supreme, God the Ultimate, and the Absolute unite as one. The Urantia Book says that this second-level union has already been revealed a little through the appearance of beings called Majeston.
p106.025: What would happen if this union were fully formed? The Urantia Book says it does not know, yet it is confident that the unknowable I AM would then be experienced as the Father. It reasons “⟦Q 106:8.22⟧that the final destiny of all personalities is the final knowing of the Universal Father of these selfsame personalities⟦/Q⟧”.
p106.027: All these unions seem like things of the far future, but in fact infinity is already united as one in the Paradise Trinity at this very moment. We feel it as something coming about little by little because of our limits as beings who live in time, space, and experience. Time, space, and experience are our greatest helps for knowing reality, and at the same time they are barriers that keep us from knowing reality fully.
p106.028: In the end, the way to succeed in the journey toward infinity is to become like the Father, and that means living the will of God. The Urantia Book says that a life lived by God's will is “⟦Q 106:9.12⟧predicated on truth, sensitive to beauty, and dominated by goodness⟦/Q⟧”. Such a person shines inwardly with worship and outwardly serves his neighbors with love and mercy. At the end of this enormous story of the universe, our task turns out to be surprisingly simple: to live today truly, beautifully, and well.
p107.002: The Universal Father lives on Paradise at the very center of the whole universe, yet at the same time he is truly present in the mind of each one of us. The way he does this is the Thought Adjuster. The Thought Adjuster is a fragment of God, given out by God himself, who lives in our minds and leads us toward God. The Urantia Book also calls the Adjuster a Mystery Monitor, and it says the Adjuster is “⟦Q 107:0.6⟧man's infallible cosmic compass⟦/Q⟧”, always pointing our souls toward God.
p107.003: God told us to be perfect as he is perfect, and so he came down himself as the Adjuster to be our companion on the way. It is also the Adjuster who stirs up within us the longing to be like God and to reach Paradise. The Urantia Book explains that, depending on a person's stage of growth, the Adjuster is also called a Thought Changer until about the age of twenty, a Thought Adjuster until about forty, and a Thought Controller after that.
p107.005: The Solitary Messenger who wrote this paper openly admits that no one can speak with authority about the nature of the Adjusters. Still, there is one thing everyone agrees on: the Adjusters are not created beings, but pure, unmixed divinity that comes directly from the Universal Father. The Urantia Book says, “⟦Q 107:1.2⟧they are of God, and as far as we are able to discern, they are God⟦/Q⟧”.
p107.006: No one knows when the Adjusters came into being or how many of them there are. We can only guess that new Adjusters keep coming forth as the universe grows larger and more people are ready to receive them. Meanwhile, the Infinite Spirit and the Creator Sons also share parts of their own spirit to become one with other orders of beings, but the Adjusters this paper talks about are the gift of the Universal Father alone.
p107.008: The Urantia Book divides the Adjusters into seven orders. There are virgin Adjusters, who come to a person for the first time; advanced Adjusters, who have gained experience by serving many times; and supreme Adjusters, who were sent anew to another person on another world because the person they had been with rejected eternal life. Supreme Adjusters are not more divine, but because they have more experience, they can do more.
p107.009: As for the fourth order, the vanished Adjusters, no one knows for sure where they are or what they do. The fifth order is liberated Adjusters, freed from their assignments, and the sixth is fused Adjusters, who have become one with a human being and are that person's eternal partner. The seventh order, personalized Adjusters, are Adjusters who worked with a Paradise Son or served in an especially outstanding way, and they receive personality of their own.
p107.011: The work of the Adjusters centers on a secret world of Paradise called Divinington. No one has ever been there except the Adjusters and other entities of the Father. High spirit beings receive three commands: honor those who are senior to you, be considerate of the shortcomings of those who are junior to you, and do not try to land on Divinington.
p107.012: The writer does not regret being unable to go to Divinington, because he believes that if there were anything there truly needed for his own growth, it would not have been forbidden. Judging from the courage and wisdom the Adjusters show, they seem to receive deep training on Divinington. Personalized Adjusters are called by names, not numbers, and become teachers there.
p107.014: Because the Adjuster is a fragment of the Universal Father, it is limited in extent but absolute in its essence. That is why The Urantia Book calls the Adjusters the “⟦Q 107:4.2⟧qualified absolute fragments of the Father⟦/Q⟧”. The Adjusters have never once been disloyal to the Father. An Adjuster can be seen only by personalized Adjusters; other beings only dimly sense the light that its presence gives off. In our universe this light is called the “⟦Q 107:4.5⟧pilot light⟦/Q⟧”.
p107.015: The Urantia Book asks us a question: do we really understand what it means that a fragment of the infinite God lives within us and wants to become one with us? There are no limits to such an amazing partnership, and the Adjuster will go on showing us the wonders of God forever.
p107.017: Because we think of mind as something that connects spirit and matter, it is hard for us to understand that the Adjuster has a mind. That is because the Adjuster comes from a level before spirit and energy were separated. But since the Adjuster can plan, work, and love, it clearly has something like the ability of mind. The Urantia Book explains that the mind of the Adjuster is the same kind as the mind of the Universal Father and the Eternal Son. Even after fusion with a human being, the Adjuster's mind stays distinct from the human mind for some time.
p107.019: The Adjuster is pure spirit, but it is more than spirit. The Urantia Book says that all that can surely be said about the Adjusters is “⟦Q 107:6.1⟧that they are truly Godlike⟦/Q⟧”. The Adjuster is our eternal possibility, and we are the Adjuster's possibility of gaining personality. The Adjusters truly love us, and they long for the day when our minds become like God and we become one together.
p107.020: Within the Adjuster there is not only spirit but also an element of pure energy. That is why the Adjuster can travel across the whole universe in an instant along the gravity circuit of Paradise. The Adjuster works without rest, and it does not need to take in energy the way we take in food, because the Adjuster itself is the highest energy.
p107.022: The Adjuster is not a person, but it is a true reality, the purest divine presence in the universe. Then how can an Adjuster, which is not a person, choose a human being on its own and decide to live within him? The Urantia Book says this is a question that no being in the universe has been able to answer exactly. Since the Adjuster comes because it wants to, plans our eternal life, and loves us, it clearly has will.
p107.023: Even so, the Adjuster follows our will and does not go against it, because in the universe what is not personal always responds to the choices of personality. The Urantia Book says that the best way to describe the Adjuster is as prepersonal. And the honor of receiving an Adjuster is given only to evolutionary creatures like us, who are growing toward Paradise. Knowing that there is a fragment of God in my mind who always loves me and leads me is the surest strength when I feel lonely and shaken.
p108.002: The Thought Adjuster, the fragment of God who lives in our minds, comes to show us the Universal Father and to actually become our Father. The Adjuster's goal is to lift up our minds and lead our immortal souls all the way to the perfection of Paradise. In this way a new being is born, in which the Adjuster and the human being are one forever.
p108.003: God is perfect, but he cannot know by experience what he has not gone through himself. So the spirit of the Father comes down from Paradise and goes through every part of life together with us. In this way the infinite God truly becomes our experiential Father.
p108.005: All Adjusters are the same in divinity, but they differ according to their past experience with human beings. It seems that all Adjusters come as volunteers. Before volunteering, they already receive information about a person's ancestors, future life, intellectual abilities, and spiritual possibilities. What an Adjuster looks at most closely is the person's ability to think, the spiritual ability to recognize God, and how well these two can work together.
p108.006: When several Adjusters volunteer, the one best suited is chosen, and before leaving it is trained in the best way to reach that person's mind. Whether the person is a man or a woman makes no difference. The Urantia Book reveals that it takes an Adjuster about 117 hours to travel from Divinington to earth, and that almost all of that time is spent on registration.
p108.008: The Adjuster comes when a child makes his first moral choice. On earth, it comes on average a little before the sixth birthday. For this, the child's mind must have been prepared with the help of the adjutant spirits: it must have the desire to worship and must know how to choose between good and evil. Since Jesus came to this earth and the Spirit of Truth was poured out at Pentecost, an Adjuster comes to every normal person who can make moral judgments. There is no go-between between God and man.
p108.009: Before the Spirit of Truth came, the time when an Adjuster arrived varied with many conditions. Adjusters often came when a guardian angel was assigned or when a person made a spiritually important decision. In particular, an Adjuster never failed to come to those who loved their neighbors and served them unselfishly, and to those who quietly decided to do the will of the Father in heaven.
p108.011: The Adjusters seem to be directed from Divinington itself, and the same kinds of Adjusters work throughout the whole universe. The number and order of each Adjuster are recorded at the superuniverse headquarters, and a human being receives his true universe name only after becoming one with his Adjuster. On worlds that a Paradise Son like Jesus has visited, a personalized Adjuster is assigned to oversee the Adjusters.
p108.012: A high supervisor who came recently to look over the earth showed deep respect for the Adjusters. He praised them, saying that they had never wavered in any crisis, had never once been accused, and had been the guardians of goodness on this troubled planet. And he said, “⟦Q 108:3.6⟧I all but worship you!⟦/Q⟧”
p108.014: The Adjuster seems to work alone in our minds, but in fact it works in perfect harmony with other spiritual helpers, such as the adjutant spirits, the Holy Spirit, and the Spirit of Truth. The Father has handed over the running of the universe to his Sons, but through the Adjusters he is directly present in the mind of every creature and draws them to himself.
p108.015: Even when a world is cut off from communication with the universe because of rebellion, the communication of the Adjusters is not blocked. Earth too was isolated after the Caligastia rebellion, but contact through the Adjusters could go on.
p108.017: The Adjuster has the hard job of receiving spiritual teaching and passing it on to our material minds. Even the truths we cannot accept now are not thrown away but carefully kept so they can be used in the next life. Even angels can sometimes lose their way, but the Adjuster never wavers.
p108.018: The Adjuster is not a helper who does our thinking for us; it is one who adjusts our thinking. The Adjuster's work is not to make this life easy but to prepare us for the eternal adventure. So it may even make life fittingly hard so that we will make more decisions. We should not expect it to soothe our hurt feelings or comfort our wounded pride. Even so, the Adjuster gives us a deep peace and calm of mind.
p108.019: The Adjuster wants to change our fears into love and trust, but it cannot do this by force; that is our part. When we make a decision to break free from fear, the Adjuster uses it as a stepping-stone to lift us higher. The Urantia Book says, “⟦Q 108:5.10⟧You have perfect guides⟦/Q⟧”.
p108.021: It is amazing humility that a perfect Adjuster chooses on its own to come and live in material beings like us. The Adjuster suffers because of our selfish thoughts and foolish fears, yet it does not leave us. The “⟦Q 108:6.3⟧image of God⟦/Q⟧” that the Bible speaks of does not mean an outward likeness; it means that the spirit of the Father is within us.
p108.022: The Adjuster takes the good thoughts our minds produce and copies them over, one by one, in spiritual form, slowly reshaping our true selves for the time of resurrection. This is the growing immortal soul. Just as our parents are the parents of our bodies, the Adjuster is the divine parent who gives birth to the better person we will be in the future. Even when clouds cover the sky above us, if we believe that the Adjuster is within us, we can look beyond the fog of worry to the sun of righteousness shining brightly.
p109.002: The Thought Adjuster, the fragment of God who lives in our minds, grows too. Just as a child learns what he will do as a grown-up by playing with his friends, the Adjuster plans and practices in our minds what it will do in the next life, the morontia career, the stage between matter and spirit. Our life on earth is a practice period in which the Adjuster prepares for a greater future. That is why the Adjuster cares more about our eternal future than about the things of this world.
p109.004: Adjusters come after being trained on Divinington, and if the person they were with rejects eternal life, they go back and receive longer training. The Urantia Book says, “⟦Q 109:1.3⟧Actual living experience has no cosmic substitute.⟦/Q⟧” However perfect its divinity, an Adjuster can gain experience only by actually living it. So the Adjusters, too, grow from less experienced stages to more experienced ones as they gather experience.
p109.005: While we grow upward from man toward God, the Adjuster grows downward from God toward man. And when the two meet and become one, a being is born who is forever both a son of man and a son of God. In building the immortal soul, the Adjuster is an equal partner with our minds.
p109.007: The Urantia Book introduces a special kind of Adjuster called a self-acting Adjuster. These are Adjusters who have a lot of experience, or whose person has grown greatly in spirit, or whose person has sincerely decided to follow the will of God. Such an Adjuster may leave the body for a while as the person sleeps, to help with spiritual work in the universe.
p109.008: Because the Adjuster is not part of our body but a divine addition to it, it can leave the body if it wishes. Even so, once it has come in, it very rarely leaves even for a short time. An Adjuster that has finished all its work and is only waiting for the person's life to end is called a superactive Adjuster.
p109.009: 3. Relation of Adjusters to Mortal Types
p109.010: The way Adjusters work differs a little depending on the kind of world. On some worlds the Adjuster stays only for a while to gain experience, and on others it is loaned for one lifetime, helping the person a great deal without ever becoming one with him. People on those worlds gain eternal life in a different way. And on worlds like our earth, the Adjuster and the person enter into a betrothal on which life and death depend, and if the person survives, the two become one forever.
p109.011: The Urantia Book explains that among the early human races on earth, the ability to receive Adjusters varied. But even when the first Adjusters were with people who did not reach eternal life, they gained valuable experience and used it on other worlds. The Urantia Book says, “⟦Q 109:3.2⟧Nothing of survival value is ever lost in all the wide universe.⟦/Q⟧”
p109.013: Animals can share feelings, but they cannot exchange thoughts and ideals. It is thanks to the Adjuster's help that people can share deep thoughts and spiritual fellowship with one another. The Adjuster is not a person, but because it comes from the source of personality, it makes human personality richer. The great intellectual and spiritual leaders of history had such a great influence also because the Adjusters within them were outstanding and highly experienced.
p109.014: If the Adjusters were to leave people, the world would slowly slide back into primitive times. The writer tells us that an experienced Adjuster that had worked in fifteen people before is now showing great power in one person on earth. The experience lost by those who rejected eternal life is now benefiting this person and the whole world.
p109.016: When we use our imagination freely and rightly, or while we sleep, the Adjuster sometimes turns the stream of our thoughts in a spiritual direction. At times our minds may become clear enough to faintly hear the divine voice that is always speaking within.
p109.017: But a mind that is easily shaken, rigid thinking, and old prejudices get in the way of the Adjuster's work. In this world today we must stay loyal to God while also coming to terms with many practical matters, so we easily get worn out. Even so, for anyone with a normal mind, no inborn condition can prevent final spiritual achievement. It may be delayed a little, but when we cooperate with the Adjuster, an immortal soul is sure to grow.
p109.019: The Adjuster never fails, and it loses nothing of value. Even if a person rejects eternal life, the Adjuster carries away the good values gained in that life and passes them on to someone else. When an Adjuster that has been through this many times receives personality, it becomes a being that holds the good qualities of all the people it has been with.
p109.020: The Adjuster that guided Jesus' mind step by step while he lived on earth has now been personalized and leads the Adjusters of our universe. This Adjuster was also with Machiventa Melchizedek before. In every situation Jesus chose the Father's will, saying, “⟦Q 109:6.5⟧Not my will, but yours, be done.⟦/Q⟧” The Urantia Book says that such a decision is the true passport that takes a person beyond human limits to God.
p109.022: Personalized Adjusters live on Divinington and teach other Adjusters. They have both the divinity of the Creator and the experience of the creature, and they are the only beings in the universe who include the prepersonal, the personal, and the postpersonal all at once. They are wise and powerful workers who carry out the will of the Universal Father throughout the universe.
p109.023: Not long ago, when the emergency regency began on earth, three personalized Adjusters appeared on their own without anyone calling them and were among the most active workers. No one can predict their future mission. The fact that each small good decision we make today is kept forever in the Adjuster's hands is a great encouragement that our lives are never in vain.
p110.002: When imperfect beings are given freedom, mistakes and pain are bound to follow. God does not watch that pain from far away; he stays close in love and shares it with us. The Solitary Messenger who wrote this paper says that the love shown by the Thought Adjuster, the fragment of God who lives in our minds, is the most truly divine love in all the universe. The devotion an Adjuster gives to each individual is “⟦Q 110:0.2⟧touchingly sublime, divinely Fatherlike⟦/Q⟧”.
p110.004: The Adjuster does not live in an organ of the body called the brain; it lives in our minds. And even when we do not notice, it is always trying to communicate with us. The Adjuster is a safe guide who leads us through the dark and uncertain maze of our short lives, and it is a patient teacher. The writer says he hopes we will love our Adjusters more and co-operate with them more fully.
p110.005: The Adjuster cares most about our eternal future, but it is not indifferent to our health, happiness, and success on earth now. The Adjuster stays with us through any sickness or disaster. So it is a sad thing to harm on purpose the body in which the Adjuster lives. Not only things that harm the body, but also the poisons of the mind, such as fear, anger, envy, jealousy, suspicion, and intolerance, greatly hinder spiritual growth. Right now we are going through a time of getting to know our Adjusters.
p110.007: The Adjuster comes with an ideal plan for our lives. But we do not have to follow that plan; we are free to reject part or all of it. The Adjuster never forces us and always respects our will. The Urantia Book says, “⟦Q 110:2.2⟧No human being will ever be spiritualized by a divine Monitor against his will⟦/Q⟧”. Eternal life is a gift we can receive only if we want it.
p110.008: The Adjuster does not take over our thoughts; it tries to refine them spiritually so they can last forever. Within our minds there is our own personality, and there is the Adjuster that God has given. When we agree with the Adjuster's will and actually carry out that decision, at that moment we and the Adjuster are one.
p110.010: Even when the Adjuster tries to tell us something, the message is usually buried in the busy stream of our minds. Whether the Adjuster can guide us well depends less on what we say we believe than on our decisions, our determination, and our steady faith. The Urantia Book says that the secret of eternal life lies in a deep longing to be like God and a willingness to do whatever is needed to become so.
p110.011: The writer is sad that many people spend a great deal of time on small things while forgetting the most important thing of all, co-operating with the Adjuster. But co-operating with the Adjuster does not mean tormenting yourself or pretending to be pious. In fact, it goes well with living cheerfully and joyfully and with succeeding honorably on earth. “⟦Q 110:3.4⟧the ideal life is one of loving service rather than an existence of fearful apprehension⟦/Q⟧”.
p110.012: Being confused or discouraged is not, in itself, going against the Adjuster. Ignorance, doubt, and anxiety do not prevent eternal life. Only deliberately refusing the Adjuster's leading does that. We can live in greater harmony with the Adjuster when we choose to follow truth, beauty, and goodness, when we love God and try to be like him, when we love and serve our neighbors, and when we joyfully take up our responsibilities as citizens of the universe.
p110.013: 4. The Adjuster’s Work in the Mind
p110.014: The Adjuster knows much of the wisdom and truth of the universe, but it can pass on only a little, because our minds are not ready to receive it. Some of the thoughts that pop into our heads come from the Adjuster, but most are simply thoughts that had been stored deep in the mind rising up naturally. The Urantia Book says that new truth, when wrongly received, can even stir up fanaticism, and that many strange cults and religions arose because the Adjuster's messages were misunderstood and twisted. So we can leave what lies beyond our awareness to the Adjuster. The Adjuster will keep everything of value safe and bring it back to life in the next life.
p110.016: The Urantia Book tells us not to confuse the Adjuster with conscience. Conscience is a response of the human mind that tells us to do right. The Adjuster tries, beyond that, to show us what is truly right. Also, jumbled dreams are not messages from the Adjuster; they are mostly natural happenings of body and mind. That is because our feelings and desires get mixed in and badly twist whatever the Adjuster is trying to say.
p110.017: So it is dangerous to treat every new idea that comes into our minds as the voice of the Adjuster. The Urantia Book advises that it is better simply to take the Adjuster's voice as your own thought than to make the mistake of lifting up human thoughts as if they were the word of God. Most of the Adjuster's influence happens in a higher part of the mind that we are not aware of.
p110.019: The Urantia Book explains a person's spiritual growth through the seven psychic circles. When a person becomes able to make his own choices and take moral responsibility, he enters the seventh circle, and as he grows he moves up one by one toward the first circle. When he reaches the third circle, a guardian angel is assigned, and the Adjuster's work becomes much more active. When he reaches the first circle, he has the closest relationship with the Adjuster possible on earth, and the Adjuster can communicate with him somewhat directly.
p110.020: To move up through these circles, body, mind, and spirit must grow evenly. If only the intellect races ahead, or if spiritual zeal goes too far, it is easy to misunderstand the Adjuster's leading. When we have clean living habits, a steady body, and a balanced mind, we can safely receive the most light and truth.
p110.021: Every decision we make either hinders or helps the Adjuster's work. Important decisions are needed, but it is also important to repeat good decisions many times until they become habits. And a person in a lower circle can know God just as truly, and feel just as much that he is a child of God, as a person in a higher circle.
p110.023: Completing the seven circles does not mean becoming one with the Adjuster right away. To become one, our will must be in full agreement with the will of God. The rare person who becomes one with the Adjuster while still on earth does not pass through death; he disappears as if “⟦Q 110:7.2⟧in chariots of fire⟦/Q⟧” and is taken to the next world. When we become one with the Adjuster, all the experiences and memories of both belong to each other, and we become one new personality forever.
p110.024: Most people become one with their Adjusters only after death. The Urantia Book says that so few people truly think deeply that the spiritual call of the Adjuster is hard to hear. Not long ago one Adjuster passed on a request to the person it lived in: to do the assigned work more joyfully, to bear trials more patiently, and never to give up until the end. And it said, “⟦Q 110:7.10⟧On the human will our achievement of personality depends.⟦/Q⟧” The Adjuster within me is still believing in me and waiting for me today.
p111.002: In our minds lives the Thought Adjuster, a fragment of God, and what we grow together with that Adjuster is the soul. The soul belongs to morontia, the stage between matter and spirit, and it is our new self, which can survive even after death. That is why science or philosophy alone cannot fully understand the soul; it can be truly known only through spiritual insight.
p111.003: For a long time people have sensed that something that will last forever is growing inside a human being. Primitive people thought the soul was in the blood, the breath, or the shadow, and the teachers of India, with their idea of the atman, came close to recognizing the Adjuster correctly. The ancient Egyptians believed that a guardian spirit called the ka guided a person throughout life. One Egyptian ruler even confessed that he had succeeded greatly because he followed the guidance of the ka within him.
p111.005: The Adjuster's work is spiritual, but that work is always done in the field of our minds. The body was given through evolution and the Adjuster was given by the Father, but the mind has been placed in our hands. The mind is the stage on which we choose God or turn away from him. The Urantia Book says that what we want to understand matters more than what we understand now, and that what we are becoming day by day matters more than what we are now.
p111.006: The mind is like a musical instrument. Depending on our will, it can make discord, or it can make a beautiful melody of oneness with God. The Urantia Book also uses this comparison: “⟦Q 111:1.9⟧Mind is your ship, the Adjuster is your pilot, the human will is captain.⟦/Q⟧” The Adjuster does not force the ship along against our will. When we, the captain, trust and follow the pilot, the Adjuster carries us safely past the obstacles of time and space to the Paradise Father.
p111.008: The Urantia Book compares our minds to a loom. On that loom the Adjuster weaves in, thread by thread, the patterns of lasting values and divine meanings. What comes out of this weaving is our character, the surviving soul.
p111.009: The soul is made of three things: the human mind, the divine spirit living within it, and the relationship between the two. The soul is not simply mind and spirit added together, but an entirely new and unique value. The soul grows where our longing to know God meets God's longing to know us.
p111.011: Our mistakes and wrongdoing can slow the growth of the soul, but they cannot stop it once it has begun. Still, we are always free to reject eternal life. Becoming one with the Adjuster means that we have chosen to do the Father's will forever. The soul is like the seed of the new personality we will wear in the next world after we die.
p111.012: The Urantia Book says that our life on earth and the growth of the soul are “⟦Q 111:3.5⟧not so much a probation as an education⟦/Q⟧”. The more our souls are filled with truth, beauty, and goodness, the more they become beings that can never be destroyed. And The Urantia Book promises that good work begun in time, if it is worth finishing, will surely be finished in eternity.
p111.014: Meanings and values can be recognized only in our inner world, not in the material world outside. All the progress of true civilization is born in this inner life. That is why The Urantia Book warns that if most of the young people of a generation chase only material things, civilization is in danger. What is needed is interest in ethics, philosophy, art, religion, and the universe.
p111.015: Just as snowflakes are all six-sided yet no two are alike, each person is unique. Happiness and joy, too, come from the inner life, and no one can enjoy true joy in isolation. We cannot change everything in our surroundings, but in our inner world we are far freer to create. But if the stage of the imagination is filled with prejudice, hate, fear, resentment, and revenge, how can it bear good fruit?
p111.016: The Urantia Book says that the world today is being led by people who have plenty of ideas but too few ideals. Free creative power can also turn into a destructive force, and evil is creative power twisted toward destruction. We cannot change the past, but we can change the future through the creative efforts going on within us now.
p111.018: Doing the will of God means being willing to share our inner life with God. Sharing is Godlike. God first placed a fragment of himself within us and entrusted it to our will. The Urantia Book says, “⟦Q 111:5.2⟧The imitation of God is the key to perfection⟦/Q⟧”.
p111.019: Choosing God's will is not giving up my will; rather, it widens my will, makes it shine, and makes it perfect. The Urantia Book says that this choice consists less in the negation “⟦Q 111:5.6⟧Not my will but yours be done⟦/Q⟧” than in the positive affirmation “⟦Q 111:5.6⟧It is my will that your will be done.⟦/Q⟧” When we choose this way, the eternal partnership of man and God begins.
p111.021: Human beings are part of nature, yet they are able to rise above nature. They are finite, yet within them is a spark of the infinite. Because of these two sides, we often feel anxious and are tempted. The Urantia Book explains that being finite is never evil in itself; evil and sin arise when finite things are misused and twisted.
p111.022: Science gives us facts, and facts, combined with the experience of living, become the bricks of wisdom. When we discover the law of God and the love of God together, we begin to understand God more deeply. The Urantia Book says that of all the dangers that threaten us, pride is the greatest. Courage is fine, but self-centeredness destroys itself. “⟦Q 111:6.10⟧Pride goes before a fall.⟦/Q⟧”
p111.024: The adventure toward Paradise is a journey in which uncertainty and security go together. We do not know what will happen next, but the security that comes from trusting a loving Father does not waver. The Adjuster cannot take away the difficulties of our lives for us. But if we allow it, it fights with us and for us while we work, worry, and struggle. The Urantia Book gently asks why we do not allow the Adjuster to light up our thinking spiritually.
p111.025: The Urantia Book explains that because the people of earth come from many origins mixed together in complicated ways, it is hard for Adjusters to work here. One guardian angel reported that the person in her care was constantly torn between laziness and fear, sorrow and sickness. Even so, thanks to the Adjuster's unchanging help, that person achieved a fair amount of happiness and success and has now gone on to the next world. Our lives, too, may be shaky and hard, but with the Adjuster within us they are never in vain.
p112.002: Our earth, Urantia, is the starting point of an eternal journey. Here we begin life together with the Thought Adjuster, the fragment of God who lives in our minds. If we faithfully run the race of faith, someday we will become one with the Adjuster forever, and we will see that our present life was the entrance to that great journey. All through that long journey there is one part of us that never changes, and that is personality.
p112.003: The Urantia Book says that personality is hard to define, but it tells us a few known facts. Personality is a gift from the Universal Father; it stays unchanged through all changes; and it is absolutely unique. No two personalities in the world are the same. Personality recognizes and responds to other personalities, and it can offer God the gift of choosing, by free will, to do his will. And personality can continue beyond death in the surviving soul.
p112.005: Personality was made to be able to work anywhere, from the very lowest worlds to the very highest. The Urantia Book explains that personality has dimensions such as length, depth, and breadth. Length means growing forward, depth means values, and breadth means insight.
p112.006: Life is a process that goes on between me and my surroundings, and personality gives this relationship the continuity of an ‘I.’ Human beings are social creatures who cannot live well alone. The Urantia Book says it is literally true that “⟦Q 112:1.16⟧No man lives unto himself⟦/Q⟧”. Personality is the center that unites all the activities of our body, mind, and spirit.
p112.008: A child lives first and only afterward thinks about his life. In the same way, the facts of life come first and the explanations come later. The event of God becoming a man and coming to this earth changed the value of human personality forever. True love respects the whole personality of the other person, and when a person loves another unselfishly, all the powers within him become one with spiritual power.
p112.009: The Urantia Book says that the very fact that we have personality is evidence that we are spiritual beings. There is a great gap between matter and thought, and consciousness cannot be explained by the workings of matter alone. Science observes the material world, philosophy examines those observations, and religion directly experiences a reality beyond all of this. “⟦Q 112:2.13⟧In time, thinking leads to wisdom and wisdom leads to worship⟦/Q⟧”.
p112.010: Surviving death means moving the center of the ‘I,’ which was tied to the body, over to the eternal morontia soul. Morontia means the stage between matter and spirit. This move is made through the sincerity and persistence of our decision to seek God.
p112.012: The Urantia Book explains that there are three kinds of death. The first is spiritual death, which happens when a person finally rejects eternal life. Then, even though the body is still alive, in the eyes of the universe the person is already dead. The second is the death of the mind, when the brain is so badly damaged that the mind that makes its own choices is ruined beyond repair. Even then, the soul can survive on the basis of the choices made before. The third is the death of the body that we usually know.
p112.013: When the body dies, the Adjuster goes, carrying the memories of the life, to Divinington, the home of the Adjusters, and the soul is kept in the care of an angel called the guardian of destiny. Later the two meet again on the mansion worlds, the worlds where we first wake up after death, and they awaken us. Until then the dead person is unconscious, as if in a deep sleep, and cannot exchange messages with the people on earth.
p112.015: When death comes, the Adjuster says farewell and leaves for Divinington. The record of the life the Adjuster leaves behind is used, together with the angel's record, when the person is judged. A person who has grown a great deal spiritually can wake up on the mansion worlds right away, and those who have not wake up together with many others at the end of an age.
p112.016: If its human partner is to wake up later, the Adjuster takes on various temporary assignments in the meantime, such as observing Paradise or learning and teaching in the schools of Divinington. If the person survives right away, the Adjuster goes before the Universal Father and then returns to prepare to greet the person who is about to awaken.
p112.018: Personality is an eternal gift from the Universal Father, but whether that personality will remain an ‘I’ forever is something we must choose. Energy cannot choose, but a human being decides his own destiny. The Adjuster is the way to Paradise, but walking that way is up to our free will. This power of choice is our greatest opportunity and our greatest responsibility.
p112.019: The government of the universe always judges in favor of the person. Even if someone could not grow enough on earth for reasons that were not his own fault, more chances are given if he sincerely wants to survive. Everyone will have at least one real chance to make a final choice with full and clear understanding.
p112.020: What survives death is the soul. The soul is like a child born of us humans and the divine Adjuster together. In the resurrection halls a new morontia body is prepared, the Adjuster returns, and the angel places the soul in that body, and then we wake up again. At first the old life will seem like a faint dream, but little by little it becomes clear. Memories with no spiritual value fade away, but memories of love and friendship between people last forever, so that on the mansion worlds we will recognize our old friends.
p112.022: Just as a butterfly comes out of a caterpillar, our true personality is revealed for the first time on the mansion worlds. On earth someone may be beautiful on the outside but not on the inside, but in the morontia life, the higher we go, the more the outward form comes to look just like the inner person.
p112.023: Instead of the seven adjutant mind-spirits that helped the mind on earth, in the morontia world the cosmic mind helps us directly. To bring back the memories of our former life, the Adjuster is needed. The character we built on earth by choosing truth, beauty, and goodness becomes the foundation of the new life.
p112.025: Someday we will become one with the Adjuster forever, and this is called fusion. Fusion happens after it is confirmed that we have chosen eternal life finally and irreversibly. It usually takes place in our system, where the mansion worlds are, and once we have become one in this way, there is no longer any danger of losing eternal life. From then on, no one can tell the person and the Adjuster apart.
p112.026: The Urantia Book says that it is not that the Adjuster or the person won out over the other, but that the two together became a new being. They will pass through Havona, see the Father on Paradise, and become the Corps of the Finality, caring for the outer universes that are still being organized. The Urantia Book says that although our bodies came from the dust, “⟦Q 112:7.19⟧if you actually will, if you really desire⟦/Q⟧”, this whole heritage will be ours. It would be good to remember that each sincere choice we make now is shaping the person we will be forever.
p113.002: This paper is about guardian angels. Seraphim are the heavenly beings we usually call ‘angels.’ They are ministering spirits who live near human beings and help them in many ways. The angels people have known about since ancient times were almost all guardian angels, and they have worked on our world ever since human minds first began to awaken.
p113.004: The story of guardian angels is not a made-up myth. Jesus himself said of little children, “⟦Q 113:1.1⟧their angels do always behold the presence of the spirit of my Father⟦/Q⟧”. The Urantia Book explains that angels were first assigned by races, but since Michael came to this world, they are assigned according to a person’s intelligence, spirituality, and destiny.
p113.005: The human mind grows inward through seven circles. In the seventh circle, the outermost one, one angel together with a company of cherubim, the angels’ helpers, looks after a thousand people, and as the circles move inward, the number of people cared for by one pair of angels gets smaller. When a person reaches the third circle, or makes the supreme decision to become like God, or joins a special group called the reserve corps of destiny, from then on a pair of angels cares for that person alone. People whose minds find it hard to judge and decide for themselves also have their own groups of angels, who make sure that justice and mercy reach them amid the hardships of life.
p113.006: The Urantia Book explains that we start from the outermost circle and move inward one circle at a time as we work at understanding ourselves, governing ourselves, and mastering ourselves. The first circle, the innermost one, is the stage of close communion with the Adjuster within us. Seen this way, the angels’ care comes closer and closer the more we grow.
p113.008: An angel who is assigned to one person alone is called a guardian of destiny. The first person on earth to receive a personal guardian was Rantowoc, a wise man of the red race long ago. Every guardian of destiny is chosen from among the angels who volunteer, and the job goes to experienced, tested angels. In one example The Urantia Book gives, more than a hundred angels applied to be the guardian of a single person.
p113.009: Angels feel deep affection for the people they care for. They share most of the feelings we have, but there is one thing they find hard to understand: how easily people who have faith are still pushed around by fear and worry. One angel of the pair always works close by, while the other keeps records or rests, and they take turns.
p113.011: One of the most important things a guardian angel does is to bring together the many kinds of spiritual help that reach the human mind. Within us work the Thought Adjuster, the gift of the Father; the Spirit of Truth, the gift of the Son; and many helps that come from the Infinite Spirit. The angel coordinates these so that we can receive them better, and links the love of the Father with the mercy of the Son.
p113.012: That is why it is also the guardian angel who keeps watch over a person’s soul after death until the person wakes up again. The Urantia Book does not know exactly how the angels manage such a complex task, but it guesses that it is thanks to the unseen activity of the Supreme Being.
p113.014: If the Adjuster works inside our minds, the angel works from the outside. The angel helps us make better decisions through our social and moral surroundings. The Adjuster is our eternal essence, and the angel is the teacher of the growing self.
p113.015: Following an angel’s leading does not make life easy. Instead, we meet the steep hills of moral choice and spiritual growth, and with courage we climb over them. The Urantia Book says that the urge to pray that God-conscious people often feel frequently comes from the influence of angels. The Adjuster and the angel do not seem to communicate directly, yet they always work together in wonderful harmony.
p113.017: Angels never invade the human mind or manipulate the will. No angel has the authority to take away our freedom to choose. Angels care about us so much that, speaking in a figure, you could say they weep over our stubbornness. Of course angels have no bodies or wings, but they do have spiritual feelings.
p113.018: An angel is not a being who rules over us but one who guards us. When we choose our own path, the angel helps us make the best use of it. Ordinarily angels do not interfere in daily life; they step in only rarely, in emergencies or when they receive special orders from their superiors. With the help of the midwayers and the physical controllers they can work in the material world, but this is very unusual. Yet when a link vital to the progress of humanity was in danger, angels have sometimes stepped in on their own to help. In caring for us this way, the angels are getting to know ahead of time the companions they will work with forever.
p113.020: When a person dies, the guardian angel faithfully keeps the person’s records and soul, which means all the values that make up the real person. Then the angel goes to the first mansion world and waits for that person to awaken. In the resurrection halls the Adjuster recognizes us, the angel reassembles us as a personality, and then the angel introduces us again to the Adjuster who was with us on earth.
p113.021: If a person had a personal guardian and still did not survive in the end, the angel reports all the records, is declared free of responsibility for that failure, and then takes on a new assignment. When an age ends, waking up many sleeping people at once is the work of the group guardians. The Urantia Book explains that the guardians who sided with the rebellion during the Lucifer rebellion remain on Jerusem until the final judgment, even though many of them have truly repented.
p113.023: At the first moment of waking on the mansion world, we will see for the first time, face to face, the angel companions who were always beside us on earth. This is truly a glorious awakening and a real resurrection. After that, the angels travel with us and help us through Edentia and Salvington all the way to the headquarters of the superuniverse.
p113.024: For seraphim, the surest path to Paradise is to guide one person safely all the way to the gates of Paradise, so being a guardian of destiny is the assignment angels value most. The friendship formed on earth between a human being and an angel is never forgotten, and some guardians become our fellow finaliters in eternity. Knowing that someone unseen cares about me and watches over me is a great reason to choose courage instead of fear.
